source_findings.observed_failure: The target field state matched the expected 20-byte value and SHA, paired target/sibling/focus and refresh checks passed, and three fresh screenshot probes were captured; exact full-value OCR failed closed. Clipboard neutralization and request-marker cleanup passed, the expected-abort canary passed, and no save was attempted.
source_findings.candidate_crop_observation: The report identifies source=label-offset-fallback and a 250x32 crop at left=113, top=73 in the 800x600 screenshot. Same-run paired diagnostics place the target field at approximately x=121.7..351.7, y=79..98 and the sibling at x=504.2..664.2, y=79..98. The saved screenshot visibly contains the exact expected path; the fixed crop starts above the target field and reaches the beginning of the sibling label, so clipped helper text and sibling-label pixels are confirmed crop contamination. This is a definite crop-design weakness and plausible OCR contributor, but root cause is not proven because the report records only limited per-probe OCR output and no OCR tool versions.
source_findings.harness_design_gap: Linux uses coordinateSpace=window, while target-field candidate extraction is currently gated on coordinateSpace=desktop. The crop therefore falls back to a fixed label offset and is checked for generic bounds, not target-rectangle containment or sibling/helper exclusion. The report lacks screenshot-bracketed target/sibling geometry, focus/value/refresh snapshots, per-probe/per-PSM OCR results, and Tesseract/ImageMagick versions.
